sets.ref: published, Steer, Microwave and RF Design III section 6.4: 100 Ω to 1700 Ω at 900 MHz: Q = √(1700/100−1) = 4, X_s = 4·100 = 400 Ω, X_p = 1700/4 = 425 Ω; L = X_s/(2πf) = 400/5.654867e9 = 70.7 nH (published 70.7 nH), C = 1/(2πf·X_p) = 0.416 pF (published 0.416 pF)

published, ANU ENGN4545 notes (after Bowick, RF Circuit Design, example 4-1): 100 Ω to 1000 Ω at 100 MHz: Q = √(10−1) = 3, X_s = 300 Ω, X_p = 333.33 Ω; L = 300/(2π·1e8) = 477 nH (published 477 nH), C = 1/(2π·1e8·333.33) = 4.77 pF (published 4.8 pF)

published, Frenzel, Electronic Design 2012: 10 Ω to 50 Ω at 76 MHz: Q = √(5−1) = 2, X_s = 20 Ω, X_p = 25 Ω; L = 20/(2π·7.6e7) = 41.9 nH (published ≈ 42 nH), C = 1/(2π·7.6e7·25) = 83.8 pF (published ≈ 83.8 pF)

published, Frenzel, Electronic Design 2012: 50 Ω to 5 Ω at 433 MHz (source above the load): Q = √(50/5−1) = 3, X_s = 3·5 = 15 Ω, X_p = 50/3 = 16.667 Ω; L = 15/(2π·4.33e8) = 5.51 nH (published ≈ 5.52 nH), C = 1/(2π·4.33e8·16.667) = 22.05 pF (published ≈ 22 pF)

published, Steer section 6.4, same resistors as the low-pass example: Q = 4, X_s = 400 Ω, X_p = 425 Ω; high-pass: C = 1/(2πf·X_s) = 1/(5.654867e9·400) = 0.442 pF (series), L = X_p/(2πf) = 425/5.654867e9 = 75.2 nH (shunt)
hand, same resistors as the Bowick/ANU example: Q = 3, X_s = 300 Ω, X_p = 333.33 Ω; C = 1/(2π·1e8·300) = 5.305 pF (series), L = 333.33/(2π·1e8) = 530.5 nH (shunt)

hand: high-pass, 100 Ω to 1000 Ω at 100 MHz: C = 5.305 pF, L = 530.5 nH
